claims.claim: Arendt's political ontology in The Human Condition is rooted in a phenomenological approach derived from German Existenz-philosophy.
claims.supporting_excerpt: The political ontology explained in the book was based on a phenomenological approach rooted in the German Existenz -philosophy.

claims.claim: The search for an extraterrestrial Archimedean point represents a radical modification of the human condition, which was previously determined by Earth's circumstances.
qualifications: arising from attempts to leave our natural habitat and find an Archimedean point in the universe
claims.supporting_excerpt: The search for an ex -traterrestrial Archimedean point, Arendt argues, involves a radical modification of human condition so far having been determined by the circumstances of our native planet

definitions.definition: A human being on an existential level who is imprisoned in endless repetitive cycles of consumption and production, consuming natural goods without creating durable entities.

distinctions.distinction: The human artifice separates human existence from mere animal environment, whereas life itself remains outside this artificial world, linking man to all other living organisms.
